newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Dow Jones to include seven stocks in Taiwan index.
newsitem.headline: Dow Jones to include seven stocks in Taiwan index.

text.p: The Dow Jones World Stock Index will include seven more Taiwan shares effective from April 1, Dow Jones said in a statement on Friday.
The seven are Acer Peripherals, Asustek Computer, Inventec, Kuoyang Construction, Pou Chen, Taichung Business Bank and United World Chinese Commercial Bank, the statement said.

The seven were being added to reflect the Taiwan market's growing capitalisation and the generally higher prices of Taiwan stocks and initial public offerings, said John Prestbo, Dow Jones Global Indexes editor.
The Down Jones Taiwan Stock Index, like all others in the global indexes series, seeks to represent approximately 80 percent of the market capitalisation of the local stock market, the company said.

The Dow Jones Taiwan Stock Index is the basis of futures contracts and options on those futures that are traded on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange as well as of options contracts traded on San Francisco's Pacific Stock Exchange, it said.
The Dow Jones index began including Taiwan stock performance from April 1, 1996, a month after Taiwan began allowing foreign individuals to invest in the local stock market.
Before that, only approved foreign institutions were allowed to invest in Taiwan stocks.
